name: Bikini Kill
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: [[Kathleen Hanna]] scrawled a deodorant joke on Kurt Cobain's wall, and Nirvana turned it into the title of their biggest song. Her own band, four people from Olympia, put out three records inside a year.

eras.title: Homemade, start to finish
eras.text: Three Evergreen State College friends run a gallery, work a sandwich shop and print zines. In a town this small a band can also be a publishing house, so Bikini Kill makes everything itself first.

years.src: Olympia Music History Project · SPIN · Wikipedia
years.h: Hanna and two friends open a gallery called Reko Muse
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]], Tammy Rae Carland and Heidi Arbogast start the art and performance space in Olympia, Washington. Spoken word at Evergreen, thanks to [[Slim Moon|602432a1-35ce-40ef-90e8-c4a123d438bf]], had already put Hanna on a stage.
years.xp:
The Olympia Music History Project says Hanna co-founded the gallery in 1988. The SPIN oral history says it hosted all-ages shows, and Wikipedia says it grew out of a photo exhibit about sexism and violence that Evergreen censored.

In SPIN, Tobi Vail remembers it as a project of a collective of women in the late '80s.

years.h: Two sandwich-shop coworkers, and a zine about girls in bands
years.p: [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]] and [[Kathi Wilcox|4a0dd24b-bd17-44e0-bb0c-90238a71c720]] work the same sandwich shop in Olympia. Vail is already putting out Jigsaw.
years.xp:
SPIN's oral history dates the sandwich-shop meeting to 1989; Wikipedia dates Jigsaw to the same year. Vail had been a DJ at Evergreen's KAOS radio and played in the Go Team with K Records' Calvin Johnson before any of this.

Hanna told SPIN the Go Team mattered to her too: a stranger called Vail "the girl from the Go Team," and "It was the first time I realized I could maybe make music too."

years.cap: Bikini Kill live at the Mushroom House, Olympia
years.h: Bikini Kill starts as three friends and a borrowed name
years.p: Hanna, Vail and Wilcox form the band in October 1990. The name belonged to Olympia musician Lois Maffeo, who had used it for one act and moved on.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Vail with taking the name from Maffeo, who had used it once in the late 1980s, inspired by the 1967 B-movie The Million Eyes of Sumuru. Guitarist [[Billy Karren|7ebf8b8d-9b55-4baa-9eb7-bf8ab4be285d]] completes the four-piece; sources differ on whether he was there from the start or arrived a few months before the first US tour.

Vail told SPIN the trio began playing shows in late 1990 or early 1991. She remembers playing early practice tapes for people and thinking, "We are gonna be the most misunderstood band ever."

eras.title: Girl Night and a cassette to sell
eras.text: One year in, Bikini Kill have a cassette, a zine and a label forming down the road. A summer trip to Washington, D.C. helps give a movement its name.

years.h: Slim Moon launches Kill Rock Stars in Olympia
years.p: Moon and Tinuviel Sampson start the label with a modest aim, putting out their friends' records. It will release the band's records through the decade.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the founding to February 1991. The label later became home to [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], Elliott Smith, The Decemberists and Unwound, but Bikini Kill were the release that put it in the national press.

years.h: "Kurt Smells Like Teen Spirit" goes up on a wall in marker
years.p: After a night of drinking, [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] wrote it on [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s wall as a joke about a deodorant she and Vail had seen. [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] made it the title of their biggest song.
years.xp:
Hanna tells it in her memoir and to NPR: "I took out a Sharpie marker, and I just wrote like, 'Kurt Smells Like Teen Spirit.'" She says she wrote about ten other things on the wall that night, and Cobain called months later to ask if he could use the line in a song.

Wikipedia's account of the song says Cobain did not learn the deodorant was a product until months after the single came out, and had read it as a revolutionary slogan. Vail, who briefly dated Cobain beginning in July 1990, was with Hanna when they found the deodorant.

years.h: A cassette called Revolution Girl Style Now
years.p: Eight songs recorded at Yoyo Studios in Olympia and sold by the band. It is the only record they made before the media got involved.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the tape was recorded at Yoyo Studios across 1990-91 and runs 21 minutes and 29 seconds. The title was a slogan the band used in summer 1991 on the road to D.C. The tape was reissued on vinyl, CD and digital in 2015 by Bikini Kill Records with three bonus tracks.

years.h: A summer road trip ends at the first riot grrrl meeting
years.p: Bikini Kill and Bratmobile head to Washington, D.C., where Hanna and Jenny Toomey organize a meeting at the Positive Force house in Arlington, Virginia. Hanna also works on a zine with [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] members.
years.xp: Wikipedia's riot grrrl article describes the meeting as aimed at sexism in the punk scene. The zine is called Riot Grrrl. This is the trip on which the slogan for the demo tape took shape.

years.cap: Bikini Kill at Sylvester Park, Olympia, 1991
years.h: Bikini Kill play Girl Night at the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: At K Records' convention in Olympia, the band takes the all-female Girl Night bill alongside [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] and [[Heavens to Betsy|8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e]].
years.xp: The convention ran August 20 to 25, 1991. Wikipedia says the night brought together zine writers who had only known each other by mail and phone.

eras.title: The first record, and the first bad reviews
eras.text: Fugazi's Ian MacKaye produces the debut EP. It also brings the first wave of press, much of it hostile, and Hanna's answer to it.

years.h: Vail, Wilcox and Karren start The Frumpies on the side
years.p: [[Molly Neuman|e4832571-a120-46fb-a5ff-1350f5ed2fce]] of [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] is the fourth member of [[The Frumpies|02231403-76b1-4a4c-accc-714eda94566f]]. Hanna isn't in it.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the group toured as late as the early 2000s, including shows with the Italian punk band Dada Swing.

yt: Rebel Girl, live in Washington, D.C., 1992
years.h: Ian MacKaye produces the first Bikini Kill record
years.p: Bikini Kill is six songs and fifteen minutes cut at Inner Ear in Arlington, Virginia, with Fugazi's [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] at the board. It came out October 9, 1992 on Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp: SPIN's oral history says the songs were recorded on the spur of the moment at MacKaye's urging, the Dischord Records connection that brought the band to the D.C. area. The tracks are Double Dare Ya, Liar, Carnival, Suck My Left One, Feels Blind and Thurston Hearts the Who. Wikipedia says the EP was recorded across 1991-92.

years.h: Rolling Stone files its review of the EP
years.p: Rolling Stone's verdict on the debut, as Wikipedia's riot grrrl article quotes it. Most of the early press ran the same way.
years.xp: Hanna's answer was a self-declared media blackout, around 1992 by Wikipedia's riot grrrl article, so girls could speak for themselves without being misrepresented. Wikipedia's Bikini Kill article puts the call to 1994. Rolling Stone later reviewed the 2012 reissue too.

eras.title: Across the Atlantic, and a hero in the studio
eras.text: Bikini Kill cross the Atlantic, record with Joan Jett and finish a first album. Three records come out within a year.

years.h: Bikini Kill and Huggy Bear tour the UK
years.p: A co-headline run with [[Huggy Bear|9cf16514-25d6-46c2-8cc8-a8e857e7a3f2]], filmed by Lucy Thane as It Changed My Life: Bikini Kill in the UK.
years.xp: Thane's 30-minute film shows live footage, interviews and the Raincoats and Sister George in kitchens and club bathrooms. Huggy Bear had been thrown out of the Channel 4 show The Word on February 14, 1993 after a protest, and Melody Maker compared it to the Sex Pistols' Bill Grundy incident.

years.h: Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah splits a record with Huggy Bear
years.p: Bikini Kill take one side and Huggy Bear take the other (Our Troubled Youth). It came out March 8, 1993 on Catcall and Kill Rock Stars and holds the first recording of Rebel Girl.

years.h: Joan Jett produces New Radio and Rebel Girl
years.p: [[Joan Jett|f376828a-b438-4fda-bb2e-dcd5fbe81f83]] plays guitar, sings and produces a new single for the band. Hanna later co-writes songs on Jett's Pure and Simple.
years.xp: Hanna has called Jett's music an early example of the riot grrrl aesthetic. The three songs Jett produced later opened the 1998 compilation The Singles.

years.cap: Kathleen Hanna singing with Bikini Kill, Olympia
years.h: Hanna says the punk scene wrote Rebel Girl
years.p: She wrote the lyrics and all four members share credit. Wikipedia says artist Juliana Luecking inspired it.
years.xp:
Hanna told NPR the bandmates built the music while she made up the words on the spot, as if "the scene of punk women...really wrote that song and I just like grabbed it from the air."

Three studio versions exist: the split with Huggy Bear, the Joan Jett single, and the album take engineered by Stuart Hallerman. Rolling Stone ranked it 296 on its 2021 list of the greatest songs.

yt: Full set at Macondo, Los Angeles, April 25, 1993
years.h: Pussy Whipped is the first album
years.p: Engineered by Stuart Hallerman and released on Kill Rock Stars, it carries the album take of Rebel Girl.

eras.title: People throw things, then the band stops
eras.text: Riot grrrl is a headline and a punchline now, and the band plays rooms where people throw things. Two more records, then the end.

years.h: The first two records get squeezed onto one CD
years.p: Kill Rock Stars pairs the EP and Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah on a single disc.

years.h: "People were throwing chains at our heads"
years.p: Audiences threw things, and per Wikipedia male concertgoers often assaulted Hanna verbally and physically. She has said the band was vilified in the 1990s.
years.xp:
In Wikipedia's account Hanna said people hated them and that it was very hard to be in the band; she later said the history has mostly written this out.

In her memoir she writes about the road as a workplace: "every single night was a different set of threatened angry men." She told NPR a phrase that gets her through it is "In punk rock, there is no HR."

years.h: The Anti-Pleasure Dissertation and I Like Fucking go on 7-inch
years.p: Kill Rock Stars releases both singles in 1995. Both end up on The Singles in 1998.

years.h: Producer John Goodmanson cuts the second album in November
years.p: The sessions with Goodmanson produce Reject All American, out the following April.

years.h: The last album, Reject All American, lands on April 5
years.p: Twelve songs in under twenty-seven minutes, on Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp: Robert Christgau said Hanna and Karren added definition and confidence. Rolling Stone ranks it 19 on its 2026 list of the 100 greatest punk albums.

years.big: "We sort of lost the ability to communicate with each other."
years.h: Bikini Kill break up after seven years
years.p: Hanna's explanation to ABC News. The band split in 1997, though some listings give 1998.
years.xp: Hanna told ABC News the band was "so busy just protecting ourselves from people literally throwing stuff at us" that they stopped looking at each other and asking how everyone was doing.

eras.title: Everybody scatters
eras.text: The members split into new bands and projects. The records stay in print, but Bikini Kill is mostly a memory until the mid-2010s.

years.h: The Singles opens with the Jett sessions
years.p: Released June 23, 1998: nine tracks and 17 minutes, gathering the 1993 and 1995 single sides. Pitchfork raised its rating to a 10 on the 2018 reissue.

years.h: Hanna's solo record on a $40 drum machine leads to Le Tigre
years.p: With Johanna Fateman and Sadie Benning, she forms [[Le Tigre|2d67239c-aa40-4ad5-a807-9052b66857a6]].
years.xp: The solo album, Julie Ruin, later gave its name to her post-Le Tigre band [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]], in which Wilcox played bass.

years.h: Vail helps start Ladyfest
years.p: She is one of the founders of Ladyfest in 2000 and later plays in Spider and the Webs and The Old Haunts.

years.h: Illness takes Hanna out of Le Tigre
years.p: She leaves in 2005, and the illness is later diagnosed as Lyme disease.
years.xp: NPR reported that the undiagnosed Lyme disease kept her from performing for a stretch. She returned after treatment.

years.h: Hanna starts Bikini Kill Records to reissue the catalog
years.p: She says a revival of 90s feminism prompted it.

eras.title: Taking the catalog back
eras.text: Documentaries, reissues and a viral clip put the band back in view. The catalog ends up in the band's hands.

years.h: The Punk Singer puts Hanna's story on screen
years.p: Sini Anderson's documentary follows Hanna's career, including the Lyme disease diagnosis.

years.h: Revolution Girl Style Now gets a proper release
years.p: The demo tape comes out on vinyl, CD and digital, with bonus tracks Ocean Song, Just Once and Playground.

years.h: Vail files a copyright claim on a Hillary Clinton video
years.p: A pro-Clinton video set to Rebel Girl goes viral after John Podesta tweets it, and it comes down after Vail's notice.
years.xp: Vail said the band doesn't authorize use of its songs in advertisements. Vail supported Bernie Sanders in the primary.

years.h: Hanna, Wilcox and Vail play one song at The Kitchen
years.p: The occasion is a New York book-release event for Jenn Pelly's book on The Raincoats.

years.h: The whole catalog goes to streaming
years.p: Everything lands on Apple Music and Spotify, and The Singles is reissued on CD and vinyl.

eras.title: The room is full now
eras.text: The reunion comes with a new guitarist and none of the old fear. The crowds are bigger than they were in the 1990s.

years.h: The reunion starts at the Hollywood Palladium
years.p: Announced January 15, the first show is April 25 with Alice Bag opening. Erica Dawn Lyle plays guitar in place of [[Billy Karren|7ebf8b8d-9b55-4baa-9eb7-bf8ab4be285d]].
years.xp:
Rolling Stone calls these the group's first full shows since the 1997 breakup, with New York dates at Brooklyn Steel on May 31 and Terminal 5 on June 1. Hanna told the magazine that Bikini Kill "was a really intense, amazing band to be in" and hoped the music would be "the gateway drug to feminism."

Its story does not say why Karren was not part of it; Wikipedia says he did not take part.

years.cap: Bikini Kill at Brixton Academy, London, June 2019
years.h: The reunion lands at Brixton Academy
years.p: One of two European dates that June, with Big Joanie, The Tuts and Child's Pose in support.

years.h: Bikini Kill headline day three of Riot Fest in Chicago
years.p: The September 15 show puts the band on a festival main stage.

years.h: A 2020 tour gets announced, and then the pandemic hits
years.p: Thirteen North American dates were to begin March 13, 2020 at the Capitol Theater in Olympia. The tour moved to 2022.

years.cap: Bikini Kill live in Sao Paulo
years.h: Sara Landeau takes over on guitar
years.p: Landeau, who has played with Hanna and Wilcox in The Julie Ruin, becomes the touring guitarist.

years.h: First Australian tour in 26 years, and a drum tech steps in
years.p: Vail becomes ill during the tour. Lauren Hammel, the band's Australian drum tech and a member of Tropical Fuck Storm, plays drums at the Victorian shows.
years.xp: ABC News caught up with the band for the tour. Vail said that with today's social media, "I don't think we would have lasted more than three months." Hanna said, "It feels like we're back to an even worse place than when we started as a band in our 20s."

years.cap: Bikini Kill at the Roundhouse, London, June 12, 2024
years.h: Hanna's memoir comes out and the band tours the UK
years.p: Rebel Girl: My Life as a Feminist Punk is published by Harper Collins, and a UK tour begins June 12.
